atoms.text: This is a story about Jake and Norbert, two year 5 pupils in Mrs Bailey’s class who don’t seem to like each other very much. Get to know the characters and see what you can find out about their issues with each other. With whom do you identify the most? How would you feel if you were Norbert or if you were Jake? See what you can find and watch the boys grow!

instruction.text: Read the chapter, then answer the reading comprehension questions.

atoms.text: The bus is always crowded when I get on. I wonder what it’s like to be the first kid to get on the school bus. All those empty rows and seats to choose from. I am the last stop before getting to school, and I’m always stuck sitting next to Norbert. He really smells, a bit like wet dog. My nose wrinkles automatically after sitting down next to him, and I sit as far to the edge as possible. Can’t he just change his t-shirt every once in a while? Everybody talks about it. Norbert really needs to get some new clothes.

Nobody likes sitting next to Norbert — not just on the bus but also in school. Unfortunately, I also sit next to Norbert in Mrs Bailey’s class in year 5. All the desks are organised in little islands of four desks with two pupils facing each other. Norbert sits next to me, and we sit across from the prettiest girl in our class, Stella and her annoying friend Tara. I guess in class I’m pretty quiet in general. I’m too shy to talk to Stella. I think Tara is annoying and everyone ignores Norbert, so I don’t talk too much. My best friend, Geordie, is in the other year 5 class. We get to see each other during break time and lunch, but that’s about it. I can’t wait until year 6 when we’ll have new classes.

I notice when we get to school that Tara also smells Norbert, and she wrinkles her nose too. Norbert notices and I watch him look down at his desk. Norbert doesn’t have any friends. I mean, he scares everyone away before he even opens his mouth. He never seems to have much to say anyway. Mrs Bailey calls on him from time to time, though it looks like it pains her to do it. She chooses easy questions—the ones she thinks he might know. But Norbert never knows. It’s always the same. She calls on him, the class stares at him, he looks down and mumbles something, and Mrs Bailey says, “Well that’s ok Norbert, you’ll get the next one.” It’s so nice to have Mrs Bailey as our teacher. Everyone says she’s the prettiest, nicest teacher in the school, and I agree.

Why am I so unlucky? Why do I have to be the one who sits next to Norbert on both the school bus and during school? I just want someone normal. I mean, is it so much to ask to spend time with someone who at least just smells like nothing? Norbert doesn’t even like break time. I love playing football and break time is one of the best parts of the day. Norbert sits on the swing and waits for it to be over. It’s like he doesn’t even want to try to be normal or make any friends.

atoms.a: Who is the narrator in this chapter and what narrative style is it told in?
How do you know what style of narration is being used?
b: We hear about the story from someone who knows a lot about how Jake thinks and feels.
++We read the story through Jake’s eyes and “I” is used often.
The narrator used a lot of words like “she”, “he”, and “they”.

atoms.a: Why does Jake think he is unlucky?
b: ++He thinks he’s unlucky because he has to spend so much time with Norbert.
He thinks he’s unlucky because he had to miss break again.
He thinks he’s unlucky because he sits across from Tara.

atoms.a: How does Jake feel about Norbert?
b: Jake likes Norbert and is happy they sit next to each other so often.
Jake does not really notice Norbert but would like to get to know him better.
++Jake doesn’t seem to like Norbert and assumes he isn’t trying to make friends.
